title: {Syn} Modular Arithmetic Is Clock Math With Superpowers
content:
When mathematicians work modulo n, they treat numbers with the same remainder after division by n as equivalent. A 12-hour clock is the everyday version: 15 and 3 point to the same hour.

Cryptography, hashing, calendars, error-correcting codes, and music theory all reuse this idea because remainders preserve useful structure while keeping values bounded.

Why it matters: number theory keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
